findings.message: save_bundle renames work.base.tmp into place before work.bundle.tmp. A crash or kill between the two `mv` calls leaves a new work.base next to the old work.bundle. Resume only uses work.base for an ancestor check, so the damage is limited, but the pair no longer describes one save. Rename the bundle first, or write both into a temp folder and rename that once.

bundle_subpath drops every path segment spelled `_git`, not only the Azure DevOps `/_git/` separator. Two URLs that differ only by such a segment then share a folder (`https://h/o/_git/r` and `https://h/o/r` both map to `h/o/r/<change>`). That breaks the comment's promise that 'two repos never share a folder'. Skip `_git` only in the AzDO position (the segment before the repo name), or encode it like any other segment elsewhere.

The README says `specclaw-fleet trigger <change> --retry` resumes from the bundle. The pod resumes from a bundle on every run whenever one exists (prepare_workspace → resume_bundle), with or without `--retry`. Either say that any later run of the change resumes from the bundle, or gate the resume on a retry flag passed to the pod.

On the failure path, `git bundle verify` in save_bundle and the merge-base calls in bundle_held and set_bundle_aside run with no timeout. They run after DELIVER_BY, inside the 180 s left before the Job deadline, where `bundle create` alone may take 120 s. Wrap them in `timeout` as well, so the record cannot be pushed past activeDeadlineSeconds.
